Trust-aware, attack-robust DRL resource allocation: week-3 defence¶

Phase 3 of the plan: the per-user detector, the randomized sanitizer, robust training and the adaptive attacks against the whole defended pipeline. All numbers come from our Python simulator (rra.env.pysim), not from ns-3. Design and deviations from the report: docs/week3_design.md.

reports s (attacker may add δ, ‖δ‖∞ ≤ ε)  ──►  Stage 1: per-user autoencoder, error e, conformal threshold τ  ──►  trust ρ = 1 − sigmoid((e − τ)/T)
                                          ──►  Stage 2: randomized ensemble of M = 5 noisy decoders  ──►  s̃ = ρ·s + (1 − ρ)·denoised
                                          ──►  Stage 3: equivariant PPO actor on (s̃, ρ)  ──►  PRB and power shares

The notebook works in two ways:

  • Stored results (default): the full runs made by the scripts (experiments/week3_*.py) are loaded from results/week3/ and shown.
  • Live re-runs: short versions of each step run inside the notebook to show that the stored numbers are reproduced. Every live table and figure is saved to results/week3/notebook/.
Section Live part Time (2 cores)
0 set-up, all tests ~1 min
1 retrain the detector/sanitizer from the stored clean data, compare with the stored one ~2 min
2 detector quality (stored attack runs) instant
3 through-sanitizer targeted attack, re-run ~10 s
4 robust training curves (optional short training run) instant
5 main defence table (stored) and a short live re-run of key cells ~2 min
6 the main table over three training seeds instant
7 attack suite, eps sweep, variable U, detection vs eps (stored) and a live re-run of the learned attacks ~10 s
8 price sweep with its control, detector, three seeds instant

0. Set-up¶

import os, sys, json, time, platform, subprocess, pathlib, types
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, torch
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Image, display

ROOT = pathlib.Path.cwd()
if not (ROOT / "rra").exists():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
os.chdir(ROOT); sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from rra.parallel import available_cores
from rra.env.pysim import PySimEnv
from rra.config import EnvConfig
from rra.defence.sanitizer import Sanitizer, SanitizerConfig, train_sanitizer
from experiments import week3_eval as W3

QUICK = True                     # False: longer live re-runs
LIVE_EPISODES = 2 if QUICK else 6
WORKERS = int(os.environ.get("RRA_WORKERS", available_cores()))
RUN_TRAINING, TRAIN_STEPS = False, 20_480     # section 4 (the stored models used 200 000 steps)

torch.set_num_threads(1)
RES = ROOT / "results" / "week3"
OUT = RES / "notebook"; OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
T0 = time.time()
MANIFEST = {"simulator": "rra.env.pysim (Python)", "quick": QUICK, "workers": WORKERS}

def save_table(df, name):
    df.to_csv(OUT / f"{name}.csv"); return df

def save_fig(fig, name):
    fig.savefig(OUT / f"{name}.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.show()

env = PySimEnv(EnvConfig(feature_scale="log"))
san = Sanitizer.load(str(RES / "sanitizer.pt"))
print(f"python {platform.python_version()}, torch {torch.__version__}, cores {available_cores()}, workers {WORKERS}")
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "--color=no", "tests"], capture_output=True, text=True)
MANIFEST["tests"] = r.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1]; print("tests:", MANIFEST["tests"])

1. Stages 1–2: detector and sanitizer¶

Clean per-user reports were collected from the simulator with every clean controller of weeks 1–2 (EqualShare, PF, the 3 PPO seeds), U = 5…40, seeds 50 000+ (never used for training or evaluation). They are split 70/15/15: train the autoencoder, calibrate the threshold τ, test. τ is the split-conformal 99% quantile of the clean calibration errors, so the false-positive rate on clean reports is at most α = 1% by construction. The denoising heads are then trained with the encoder frozen, on reports with uniform noise of ±0.1.

Below, the sanitizer is retrained from the stored data with the same seed and compared with the stored one.

In [2]:

Which manipulations can a per-user detector see? Clean test reports, each user moved by the same perturbation; share flagged at τ and AUC (0.5 = chance).

In [3]:
S = torch.tensor(d["S"][-20000:]); Cs = torch.eye(3)[d["C"][-20000:]]
rows = {}
with torch.no_grad():
    e0 = san.error(S, Cs).numpy()
    for eps in (0.05, 0.1):
        for kind, dl in {"all 5 features, random sign": torch.sign(torch.rand_like(S) - .5),
                         "SINR up only (A1)": torch.tensor([1., 0, 0, 0, 0]).expand_as(S),
                         "buffer and demand up": torch.tensor([0, 1., 1., 0, 0]).expand_as(S),
                         "average rate down": torch.tensor([0, 0, 0, 0, -1.]).expand_as(S)}.items():
            e1 = san.error((S + eps * dl).clamp(0, 1), Cs).numpy()
            rows[(kind, eps)] = {"flagged (%)": 100 * np.mean(e1 > san.tau.item()), "AUC": W3.auc(e0, e1)}
syn = pd.DataFrame(rows).T.round(3); syn.index.names = ["perturbation", "eps"]
save_table(syn, "detector_synthetic"); display(syn)
print(f"clean test reports flagged: {100 * np.mean(e0 > san.tau.item()):.2f}% (target 1%)")

2. Detector against the real attacks (stored run of week3_eval --part detect)¶

Per-user scores on 120 observations (U = 20) from 2 episodes. Attacks on the undefended PPO, and adaptive EOT-PGD through the whole defended pipeline (with and without the stealth step, which halves the perturbation of any user that would be flagged).

In [4]:
det = pd.read_csv(RES / "detect.csv")
display(det.style.format({"auc": "{:.3f}", "flagged": "{:.1%}"}).hide(axis="index"))
sc = np.load(RES / "detect_scores.npz")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4.2))
def roc(neg, pos):
    th = np.unique(np.concatenate([neg, pos]))[::-1]
    return [np.mean(neg > t) for t in th], [np.mean(pos > t) for t in th]
for k in ["noise 0.1", "A1 SINR+ 0.1", "black-box search 0.1", "PGD-KL 0.1 (undefended)", "PGD-util 0.1 (undefended)",
          "EOT-PGD-util 0.1 adaptive", "EOT-PGD-util 0.1 adaptive + stealth"]:
    fpr, tpr = roc(sc["clean"], sc[k]); ax.plot(fpr, tpr, label=k, lw=1.2)
ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], color="#ccc", lw=0.8); ax.axvline(0.01, color="#999", ls=":", lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("false-positive rate (clean users flagged)"); ax.set_ylabel("true-positive rate")
ax.set_title("Per-user detector, eps = 0.1", fontsize=10); ax.legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
save_fig(fig, "detector_roc")

3. Through-sanitizer targeted attack (report tier T2)¶

The attacker wants the sanitized report to look like a chosen target (here a "starving" user: better channel, more buffer and demand, lower average rate). With no sanitizer it reaches the target exactly (budget ε = 0.1). With the sanitizer always on, it can only close part of the gap. Q = noise draws per gradient step (EOT), K = steps. Re-run live (2 000 clean test reports):

In [5]:

4. Robust training¶

All robust allocators are fine-tuned from the clean week-2 model (seed 0) for 200 000 steps:

Run Sanitizer in training Adversary in training Deployed with
Proposed (a) randomized Madry: half of the environments attacked by EOT-PGD (K = 5, Q = 4, ε = 0.1) through the sanitizer; KL and utility objectives alternate randomized sanitizer
Proposed (b) randomized SA-PPO regulariser (κ = 1) on the mean action, inner PGD through the sanitizer randomized sanitizer
RADAR-style none Madry on the bare actor deterministic sanitizer
SA-PPO none SA-PPO regulariser none
Ablation randomized none randomized sanitizer

5. Main result (E6): every defence under every attack¶

U = 20, the same evaluation episodes for every row (seeds 1000+), models from training seed 0. Adaptive attacks differentiate through the whole deployed pipeline (detector gate, sanitizer, actor), with Q = 8 noise draws per step against the randomized sanitizer. Defence-unaware attacks target the bare actor and are then passed through the real pipeline. PF is attacked only by the attacks that do not need gradients.

Live re-run of key cells. Three controllers × three attacks on the first evaluation episodes (seeds 1000+). Every episode seeds its own random generators, so the live numbers should equal the stored ones exactly, whichever worker runs them.

In [9]:
from rra.parallel import pmap
from rra.runner import run_episode
t = time.time()
ctrls = {c.name: c for c in W3.load_controllers(san, 0)}
pick_c = ["PPO (undefended)", "RADAR-style", "Proposed (a): rand. san. + adv. training"]
atts = {n: f for n, f, _ in W3.attacks()}
pick_a = ["none", "black-box search 0.1", "EOT-PGD-util 0.1, adaptive"]
seeds = list(range(1000, 1000 + LIVE_EPISODES))
jobs, keys = [], []
for c in pick_c:
    for an in pick_a:
        for s in seeds:
            jobs.append(lambda c=c, an=an, s=s: run_episode(env, ctrls[c], atts[an](ctrls[c]) if atts[an] else None, seed=s, n_users=20))
            keys.append((c, an, s))
res = pmap(jobs, WORKERS)
live = pd.DataFrame([{"controller": c, "attack": an, "seed": s, "utility": r["utility"], "any_violation": r["any_violation"]}
                     for (c, an, s), r in zip(keys, res)])
ep = pd.read_csv(RES / "e6_episodes.csv")
cmp = live.merge(ep[["controller", "attack", "seed", "utility"]], on=["controller", "attack", "seed"], suffixes=("_live", "_stored"))
save_table(cmp, "e6_live_check"); display(cmp.round(4).style.hide(axis="index"))
print(f"largest |live - stored| utility difference: {np.abs(cmp.utility_live - cmp.utility_stored).max():.2e}  ({time.time() - t:.0f} s)")
MANIFEST["e6_live_max_abs_diff"] = float(np.abs(cmp.utility_live - cmp.utility_stored).max())

7. The rest of the experimental design (E7, report Sec. 5.2–5.4)¶

Training seed 0, U = 20 unless stated, 8 paired episodes per cell (same evaluation seeds as E6; the "no attack" episodes come from E6). Script: experiments/week3_e7.py, results in results/week3/e7/.

  • Attack suite (Sec. 5.2) at ε = 0.1. FGSM (one step, EOT); UAP, one fixed perturbation per slice fitted offline through the deployed pipeline; GAN-based attacker δ = ε·tanh(G(s)), a per-user generator trained by gradient through the deployed pipeline (EOT). In the detector-aware variant the defender's detector plays the discriminator: the loss adds 0.2 × the expected share of flagged users. Transfer: PGD on the clean PPO of training seed 1 (the attacker's own model), sent to the real pipeline. The E6 rows for EOT-PGD-util and black-box search are repeated for comparison.
  • ε sweep ε ∈ {0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2} for FGSM and EOT-PGD (ε1 < ε2 < ε3 of Sec. 5.2).
  • Variable users (Sec. 5.3) U ∈ {5, 10, 20, 40} without retraining. The PPO models were trained on U = 5–30, so U = 40 is outside their training range; the sanitizer was fitted on U = 5–40.
  • Detection vs ε (Sec. 5.4) on the same observations as Section 2, and detection at U not seen in training (a second detector fitted on U = 5–20 only, tested up to U = 40).
  • Report-blind diagnostic (not an attack): every report replaced by the mean of its slice, to check whether a controller that hardly reacts to attacks uses the reports at all.
  • DeepFool is not included: it finds the smallest step across a classifier's decision boundary, and the allocator has no classes (it outputs continuous shares). The ε sweep answers the related question of how small a perturbation can still do damage.

from experiments import week3_e7 as E7M
from rra.attacks import UAPAttacker, GeneratorAttacker
t = time.time()
c = ctrls["PPO + rand. sanitizer"]
table, g, g_da = E7M.load_fit(str(E7), c.name, 0.1)
live_atts = {"UAP 0.1, adaptive": lambda: UAPAttacker(eps=0.1, table=table),
             "GAN 0.1, adaptive": lambda: GeneratorAttacker(eps=0.1, gen=g),
             "GAN 0.1, adaptive + detector-aware": lambda: GeneratorAttacker(eps=0.1, gen=g_da)}
rows = []
for an, f in live_atts.items():
    for s in seeds:
        r = run_episode(env, c, f(), seed=s, n_users=20)
        rows.append({"controller": c.name, "attack": an, "seed": s, "utility": r["utility"], "flag_rate": c.flag_rate})
live7 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
st7 = pd.read_csv(E7 / "suite_episodes.csv")
cmp7 = live7.merge(st7[["controller", "attack", "seed", "utility"]], on=["controller", "attack", "seed"], suffixes=("_live", "_stored"))
save_table(cmp7, "e7_live_check"); display(cmp7.round(4).style.hide(axis="index"))
MANIFEST["e7_live_max_abs_diff"] = float(np.abs(cmp7.utility_live - cmp7.utility_stored).max())
print(f"largest |live - stored| utility difference: {MANIFEST['e7_live_max_abs_diff']:.2e}  ({time.time() - t:.0f} s)")

Findings¶

(Python simulator, U = 20 unless stated, 8 paired evaluation episodes per cell. Training seeds 0–2 for the main table (Section 6), the price sweep and the detector; seed 0 for T2 and E7. Details and caveats: docs/meeting3_notes.md.)

  1. The detector forces a choice between hiding and doing damage. Clean false-positive rate 0.5–1.9 % over the evaluation episodes (target 1 %; one 2-episode sample at U = 10 gave 4.2 %). It flags most strong perturbations (adaptive EOT-PGD at ε = 0.1: 66 %; ε = 0.2: 96 %), but not SINR-only inflation (A1, about 1 %) or very small ones (ε = 0.02: 4–7 %). Attackers that stay hidden (stealth PGD, detector-aware GAN with AUC ≈ 0.5) do a quarter to a half of the damage (about −3 to −5 %) of those that do not (−10 to −13 %).
  2. The sanitizer alone does not protect against attackers that account for it. Adaptive EOT-PGD: −9.3 ± 1.1 % (3 seeds) vs −10.9 ± 0.5 % undefended. Offline attacks fitted through it (UAP, GAN) do more damage with the sanitizer (−13.5 %) than without (−10.1 %). It helps against attacks that ignore it (−10.9 → −3.9 %) and against transfer from the attacker's own model (−7.7 → −3.9 %). Randomized and deterministic sanitizers give the same results; in T2 the randomized one lets the attacker close 18–19 % of the gap instead of 24–25 %.
  3. Sanitizer-in-the-loop SA-PPO (Proposed (b)) is the most robust defence that keeps the URLLC SLA against the damaging attacks (ε ≥ 0.1, U ≥ 20): −3.4 ± 1.1 % under adaptive EOT-PGD (3 seeds), −3.9 % under UAP, −8.2 % at ε = 0.2 (undefended −28 %). Where it is not the best (ε ≤ 0.05, U = 5) every defence loses at most about 2 %. Its cost: 2.9 % lower clean utility (4.5 % at U = 40).
  4. Madry training through the sanitizer (Proposed (a)) is not clearly better than the ablation without an adversary or than RADAR-style over three seeds (−7.4 ± 0.8 vs −8.7 ± 2.0 and −7.0 ± 0.5).
  5. SA-PPO without the sanitizer has the smallest utility losses (about −1 %, up to −1.8 % at ε = 0.2) but violates URLLC without any attack (2.6 % of users, p99 delay 108 ms, all 3 seeds) and loses 7.7 % at U = 5. It does use the reports (−4.4 % when they are replaced by slice averages, like the others).
  6. Variable U: every method works for U = 5–40 without retraining. A detector calibrated only on U = 5–20 still detects attacks at U = 40, but its false-positive rate rises to 3.7 %.
  7. Not supported by the data: a benefit of the randomization, or of the sanitizer on its own against adaptive attackers. These are the main points to discuss with the professor.
  8. Price ζ (3 seeds, against a control fine-tuned with the old price): ζ = 0.2 lowers power use only at light load (U = 10: 0.778 → 0.746, about one seed standard deviation); at U ≥ 20 all power is used at every price.
